extended:
**A NON-COMMUTATIVE FORMULA FOR THE COLORED JONES FUNCTION**

*STAVROS GAROUFALIDIS AND MARTIN LOEBL*

22 pp, 22 sections.

**Abstract.** The colored Jones function of a knot is a sequence of Laurent polynomials that encodes the Jones polynomial of a knot and its parallels. It has been understood in terms of representations of quantum groups and Witten gave an intrinsic quantum ﬁeld theory interpretation of the colored Jones function as the expectation value of Wilson loops of a 3-dimensional gauge theory, the Chern-Simons theory. We present the colored Jones function as an evaluation of the inverse of a non-commutative fermionic partition function. This result is in the form familiar in quantum ﬁeld theory, namely the inverse of a generalized determinant. Our formula also reveals a direct relation between the Alexander polynomial and the colored Jones function of a knot and immediately implies the extensively studied Melvin-Morton-Rozansky conjecture, ﬁrst proved by Bar-Natan and the ﬁrst author about ten years ago.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 1.1 The Jones polynomial of a knot; 1.2 Statement of the main result; 1.3 Acknowledgement; 2 The zeta function of a graph and the quantum; 3 The arc-graph of a knot projection; 4 The enhanced arc-graph and the Jones polynom; 5 Proof of Theorem 2; 5.1 Row and column arcs order; 5.2 Flows on GK and monomials of GB'K(m1,…mr); 6 Cabling of the arc graph; 6.1 Comparison of excess numbers; 7 Sortings and multiplicities of flows; 7.2 Sortings and the Jones polynomial; 7.3 Proof of Theorem 7; Appendix A. The zeta function of a graph and t; A.1. The Foata-Zeilberger formula
